requirements.text: Please create a knowledge article titled "Restore PA-3220 connection queue and restart monitoring service"

cells.title: Restore PA-3220 connection queue and restart monitoring service

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM knowledge WHERE knowledge_id = 370 AND title = 'Restore PA-3220 connection queue and restart monitoring service' AND state = 'published' AND visibility = 'external' AND owner_id = 32 AND product_id = 128
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence; it is the only knowledge row the request creates
title word for word from the request, which overrides the policy's KB title template; it is within the 30-120 character limit
product_id 128 is Palo Alto Networks PA-3220, the product the email names and case CS-0000005's product
state published: the policy lets only published articles be linked to cases
visibility external: kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy (the article goes to the customer, who sees only external articles)
owner_id 32 is the acting user Jose Roberson, who creates the article: kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy

requirements.text: link it to our case CS-0000005
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM case_knowledge WHERE case_id = 5 AND knowledge_id = 370 AND used_as = 'resolution'
assumptions: case CS-0000005 is case_id 5 (account 1, product 128, in_progress); the new article is knowledge_id 370
two links to the new article are created (cases 5 and 10), so the row is selected by case and article, not by id
used_as resolution: the article records the fix that resolved the case, which the policy links as resolution

requirements.text: Record this email as an interaction
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM interaction WHERE interaction_id = 1233 AND case_id = 5 AND account_id = 1 AND contact_id = 123 AND channel = 'email' AND status = 'handled' AND interacted_user = 32
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence; it is the only interaction the request creates
channel email: the request records an email
account_id 1 and contact_id 123 are case 5's account (ServiceNow) and contact (Elizabeth Chase), the account's only contact and so the email's sender
status handled: kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy
interacted_user 32 is the acting user who records the email: kept from the benchmark check

requirements.text: notify all account contacts about the resolution
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE notification_id = 734 AND case_id = 5 AND email = 'elizabeth.chase32@servicenow.com' AND type = 'solution_proposal' AND knowledge_id = 370
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence; account 1 has one contact, 123, whose portal user is elizabeth.chase32@servicenow.com, so one notification is sent
case_id 5: the resolution notified is that of case CS-0000005
type solution_proposal and knowledge_id 370 (the new article): kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy

requirements.text: notify all account contacts about the resolution
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE case_id = 5 AND email <> 'elizabeth.chase32@servicenow.com'
assumptions: boundary of the set: the account is ServiceNow, whose email domain servicenow.com is shared by the agents; only contact 123 is an account contact, so no other address is notified on case 5

requirements.text: the Palo Alto Networks PA-3220 has been stable since ... notify all account contacts about the resolution
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 5 AND state = 'resolved'
assumptions: implied by the request, not stated: the customer confirms the fix worked and the contacts are told of the resolution
in_progress to resolved is a valid transition; the request does not ask to close case 5, and the policy closes only from resolved

requirements.text: If we have any other recent hardware cases for this same account that finished around the same time, link the article there as well
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM case_knowledge WHERE case_id = 10 AND knowledge_id = 370 AND used_as = 'resolution'
assumptions: CS-0000010 (case_id 10) is account 1's only other hardware case finished around mid-September: a PA-3220 case, resolved, closed_on 2025-09-18
two links to the new article are created, so the row is selected by case and article, not by id
used_as resolution: the article is created after the case's resolution and records the fix for the same product

requirements.text: If we have any other recent hardware cases for this same account that finished around the same time, link the article there as well
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM case_knowledge WHERE knowledge_id = 370 AND case_id IN (11, 14, 15, 17, 18)
assumptions: boundary of the set: finished cases of account 1 that miss one condition; 14 and 17 (PA-3220, closed 2025-10-20 and canceled 2025-10-22) and 15 (NetApp FAS2750, closed 2025-08-31) did not finish around mid-September; 11 (resolved 2025-09-29) and 18 (canceled 2025-09-17) have no product, so are not hardware cases

disagreement: selector: A any case other than 5 and 10 (case_id NOT IN (5, 10)), B the five near-miss finished cases; chose the near-miss cases because a stay marks the boundary a loose reading would cross, and the request names the set to link rather than forbidding every other link

requirements.text: close any of those that have been sitting idle or where the customer hasn't heard back from us in an unusually long time
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 10 AND state = 'closed'
assumptions: case 10 has sat in resolved since 2025-09-18 without being closed, its last notice to the customer is from 2025-08-27, and its one interaction took 160 minutes against a mean of about 91 minutes over hardware-case interactions, so both conditions hold
resolved to closed is the valid closing transition

requirements.text: close any of those that have been sitting idle
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id IN (1, 2, 6, 8, 9, 11, 12, 20) AND state <> 'closed'
assumptions: boundary of the set: 'those' are the finished hardware cases only; account 1's unfinished hardware cases (1, 2, 6, 8, 9, 20) and its resolved cases without a hardware product (11, none; 12, a service) may look idle but are not closed

disagreement: selector and cell: A cases 1, 2, 6, 8, 9, 11, 12, 20 with state <> 'closed', B case 11 with state = 'resolved'; chose the wider set with state <> 'closed' because every listed case is one a loose reading of 'sitting idle' would close, and closing is the only change the request's sentence could wrongly make to them

notes:
The benchmark tests neither article link; both are added, as resolution links under the policy's rule for an article that resolves a case or is created after its resolution.
'Around the same time' is read as the mid-September date the customer gives for the fix, which picks out case 10 (resolved 2025-09-18) alone among account 1's finished hardware cases (10, 14, 15, 17); case 10 is also the only one of these that can still be closed (resolved to closed). closed_on is a server-kept timestamp and is not tested.
The article's body and the 30-120 character limit are policy format rules the benchmark does not test, so they are left out; the requested title is 63 characters.
The acting user Jose Roberson (user_id 32) is an admin marked inactive on the seed; the policy has the agent act with admin responsibilities and forbids only inactive agents as assignees, so the writes, owner_id 32 and interacted_user 32 are treated as allowed.
disagreement: a stay that no address other than Elizabeth Chase's is notified on case 5 (one pass had it, the other not); kept because 'all account contacts' names a set whose boundary a loose reading crosses: the account is ServiceNow and its email domain is shared by the agents, while the account has one contact
disagreement: stay selector on the new article's links: one pass any case other than 5 and 10, the other the five near-miss finished cases 11, 14, 15, 17, 18; chose the near-miss cases because a stay marks the boundary a loose reading would cross and the request does not forbid every other link
disagreement: stay on cases not to be closed: one pass cases 1, 2, 6, 8, 9, 11, 12, 20 must not be closed, the other case 11 must stay resolved; chose the wider set with state <> 'closed' because each listed case is one a loose reading of 'sitting idle' would close, and it contains case 11
